# Kay

> Kay is a Bun web framework. A `.kay` file is one component: TypeScript fences, then a pug-like indented template. Pages render to plain HTML strings on the server, islands run on kay's own signals and DOM runtime, and an Elysia plugin serves it all with automatic islands. Everything is typed, templates included, and `kay check` reports errors at the `.kay` line and column.

## Rules that are easy to get wrong

- Every dynamic value sits in `{}`: `a(href={url})`, `p Hello {name}`. A static attribute value is a quoted string: `a(href="/about")`.
- Signals are explicit. Read `count()`, write `count.set(1)` or `count.set(c => c + 1)`. Props and server data are plain names, never called: `{title}`, not `{title()}`.
- Every `for` has a `key={...}`.
- A promise an `await` block renders is made with `defer()`, never left bare.
- The component script exports types only. Shared values live in `.ts` modules.
- A page has no props: its data comes from its `--- server` fence.
- `window`, `document`, `localStorage` and the other globals only a browser has are read in `effect` or `onMount`, or in a component whose script fence is `--- client`; reading one while rendering throws on the server.
- Indentation is spaces only, consistent within a block. Text after a tag needs one space: `p Hello`, never `p:Hello`.
- Pug features that do not exist: `- code` lines, `#{}` and `!{}` interpolation, `+mixins`, `include`, `extends`, `block`, filters, `&attributes`, `case`, `each`, `while`, `unless`, `doctype`; a line starting with one is reported, with what kay writes instead.

## File layout

Up to two fences come first, in either order, then the template. Both are optional.

```kay
--- server
const greeting = 'Hello'
---
---
import { signal } from 'kay'

const count = signal(0)
---
p {greeting}
button(onClick={() => count.set(c => c + 1)}) Clicked {count()} times
```

- `---` holds the component script: imports, props, signals, functions. It runs wherever the component renders.
- `--- server` exists on pages and layouts only. It runs on the server for each request and never reaches the browser.
- `--- client` in place of `---` makes the component render in the browser only, generic ones written `--- client <T>`; see Islands.

## Component script

Props are declared once, at the top level, with the `props<T>()` macro. It needs no import.

```kay
---
import type { Todo } from './todo'

const { todo, size = 'md', onToggle } = props<{ todo: Todo, size?: 'sm' | 'md', onToggle?: (id: number) => void }>()
---
li(class={size})
  input(type="checkbox" checked={todo.done} onChange={() => onToggle?.(todo.id)})
  span {todo.title}
```

- Destructure one level deep and read nested fields as `todo.title`; give defaults in the destructuring. A default applies only to an `undefined` prop (`null` stays `null`) and runs only then, once per component, the first time the prop is read. `const all = props<T>()` also works and reads as `all.todo`.
- Props stay reactive: the compiler turns each destructured name into a live read. They are read-only.
- Imports, `type` and `interface` declarations are module level, except a type taking the `typeof` a name the script declares, which stays inside the component. Both fences may import the same name; the server fence's copy is dropped. A fence holds TypeScript only: markup goes in the template, and JSX in a fence is reported.
- `signal(value)` from `kay` makes state; `signal<T>()` starts as `undefined`. Derived values are plain functions: `const shown = () => todos.filter(t => !t.done)`.
- `selection<Key>(initial?)` from `kay` holds one selected string or number key among many rows, or none. It reads as `selected()` and writes as `selected.set(id)`, and `selected.is(row.id)` re-runs only for the rows a change selects or unselects, not every row: `tr(class={{ danger: selected.is(row.id) }})`.
- `memo(fn)` caches a derived value until what it read changes, `effect(fn)` runs once the render is done and again whenever what it read changes, and `onMount`, `onCleanup`, `untrack`, `batch`, `root` and `flush` come from `kay` too. A write applies at once; the effects it touches run together in a microtask, or right away through `flush()`.

### Generic components

Type parameters on the script fence line make a component generic, written as TypeScript writes them; each use infers them from its props, islands included:

```kay
--- <T extends { id: number }>
const { items, show } = props<{ items: T[], show: (item: T) => string }>()
---
ul
  for item of items key={item.id}
    li {show(item)}
```

`List(items={todos} show={todo => todo.title})` types `todo` as one of `todos`, and `kay fmt` writes the line `--- <T ...>`. A page has no props, so it takes no type parameters.

## Template lines

Each line is one of the following; deeper indentation nests children under the line above.

| Line | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `tag.class#id(attributes) text` | An element. Each part is optional, but the line starts with a tag, `.` or `#`. |
| `.card` | A `div`: a line starting with `.` or `#` has an implied `div`. |
| `Card(title="x")` | A component: a capitalised tag, imported in the script. A prop, a server value or a loop item holding a component works as the tag too. |
| `\| text {expr}` | A text line, also the way to put a lone `{expr}` on its own line. Consecutive text lines are joined with a line break. |
| `// note` | A comment. Lines indented under it are commented out too. |
| `if cond` / `else if cond` / `else` | Conditional rendering. |
| `if user() as u` | Binds the truthy value to `u` for the children. |
| `for item of list key={item.id}` | A keyed list. `else` right after it renders when the list is empty. |
| `for item, i of list key={i}` | Rows matched by position. |
| `slot` | Where a layout or wrapper renders its children. |
| `@name` | Directly under a component: passes the indented block as its `name` prop. |
| `@name(a, b)` | The same, as a function of its parameters the component calls. |
| `head` | At the top level: its `title`, `meta`, `link`, `style`, `script` and `base` children go in the document head. |
| `await value` / `then name` / `catch error` | Renders the indented block under `await` until `value` settles; see Streaming. |
| `try` / `catch error` | Renders the `catch` block instead when the `try` block throws; see Error fallbacks. |

```kay
---
import type { Todo } from './todo'
import { signal } from 'kay'
import TodoItem from './todo-item.kay'

const { todos } = props<{ todos: Todo[] }>()
const filter = signal('')
const selected = signal<Todo>()
const shown = () => todos.filter(todo => todo.title.includes(filter()))
---
section.todo-list
  input(type="search" bind:value={filter} placeholder="Filter")
  ul
    for todo, i of shown() key={todo.id}
      TodoItem(todo={todo} index={i} onToggle={id => selected.set(todos.find(t => t.id === id))})
    else
      li.empty Nothing matches
  if selected() as todo
    p Selected #[strong {todo.title}]
```

### Elements

- Classes: `.class` takes Tailwind names, `:`, `/`, `@` and `!` included: `div.md:flex.w-1/2.hover:underline`. A class holding `.` or `[` goes in `class="..."`.
- `class={...}` takes a string, an array or a `{ name: boolean }` object, and merges with the `.class` shorthand and with the `class` of a `{...spread}`. A component gets what merges as one string, so its `class?: string` prop holds; an expression alone reaches it as written. An element has one `class` attribute and one id.
- Attributes are separated by spaces, inside one pair of parentheses that may span lines: `a(href="/x" target="_blank")`. A value is a quoted string or `{expression}`. A name alone is a boolean attribute. `{...obj}` spreads.
- Events are camelCase handlers: `onClick={save}`, `onInput={e => name.set(e.currentTarget.value)}`. A lowercase `onclick` or `on:click` attaches nothing, and kay reports it. A handler is read when the event fires, so one a prop, a signal or a loop item holds stays current: `button(onClick={onPress})`.
- `bind:value={signal}` on `input`, `textarea` and `select`, and `bind:checked={signal}` on a checkbox, read and write a signal both ways. On `type="number"` and `type="range"` the signal holds a `number`, and keeps its last one while the input is empty.
- `ref={el => ...}` receives the DOM element.
- Inline text follows the tag after one space. `\{` and `\#` are a literal brace and hash.
- `#[tag inline]` puts an element inside text: `p Read #[a(href="/docs") the docs] first`.
- `tag: child` nests one element on the same line: `li: a(href="/") Home`.

### Slots

```kay
---
import type { JSX } from 'kay'

const { title, actions } = props<{ title: string, actions?: JSX.Element }>()
---
article.card
  header
    h2 {title}
    | {actions}
  slot
```

A parent fills it like this: the `@actions` block becomes the `actions` prop and the other children go to `slot`.

```kay
---
import Card from './card.kay'
---
Card(title="Todos")
  @actions
    a(href="/new") New
  p Body text
```

A block taking parameters is passed as a function the component calls, once per row for instance, and its parameters take their types from the prop. A static parent cannot pass one to an island, since no function reaches the browser.

```kay
--- <T extends { id: number }>
import type { JSX } from 'kay'

const { items, row } = props<{ items: T[], row: (item: T, index: number) => JSX.Element }>()
---
ul
  for item, i of items key={item.id}
    | {row(item, i)}
```

```kay
---
import type { Todo } from './todo'
import List from './list.kay'

const { todos } = props<{ todos: Todo[] }>()
---
List(items={todos})
  @row(todo, i)
    li {i + 1}. {todo.title}
```

### Head

```kay
--- server
import { findTodo } from '../../data'

const todo = await findTodo(Number(ctx.params.id)) ?? ctx.notFound()
---
head
  title {todo.title} | Todos
  meta(name="description" content={`Todo #${todo.id}`})
h1 {todo.title}
```

- One `head` block per template, at its top level, in a page, a layout or a static component; an island has none.
- The page wins over its layouts: one `title`, and one `meta` per `name`, `property` or `http-equiv`. A `link` is one per `rel` and `href`.
- Head elements hold text only. The default charset and viewport tags can be replaced the same way.
- A `link(rel="canonical")` is one per page, the page's replacing its layouts'.

### Site defaults and social cards

`site` and `seo` in `kay.config.ts` give every page's head a starting point, which any tag a layout or the page sets replaces:

```ts
import { defineConfig } from 'kay/server'

export default defineConfig({
  site: 'https://example.com',
  seo: {
    name: 'Example',
    titleTemplate: '%s | Example',
    description: 'What the site is',
    image: '/og.png',
    twitter: '@example',
    locale: 'en_GB',
    jsonLd: [{ '@context': 'https://schema.org', '@type': 'WebSite', 'name': 'Example', 'url': 'https://example.com' }],
  },
})
```

- `site` is an origin, nothing after the host. Each page answering 200 gets `link(rel="canonical")` at `site` plus its path, query left out; an error page gets none.
- `name` is the title of a page that sets none, unwrapped, and `og:site_name`. `titleTemplate` wraps a title a layout or the page sets: `title About` renders `About | Example`.
- `og:title`, `og:description` and `og:url` repeat the page's own title (unwrapped), description and canonical link unless it sets them; `twitter:card` is `summary_large_image` once there is an `og:image`. A canonical link or an `og:image` and `twitter:image` written as a path, `/og.png` or an imported asset's URL, is made absolute against `site`. `og:type` is `website`.
- JSON-LD goes in a `head` block as a `script(type="application/ld+json")` holding its text, which `jsonLd()` from `kay/seo` writes from typed data in a server fence: `const place = jsonLd({ '@type': 'LocalBusiness', 'name': shop.name })`, then `script(type="application/ld+json") {place}`. It adds the schema.org `@context` unless the data names its own, and takes a list as one `@graph`; the type checks `@type` only, the rest being schema.org's vocabulary. Any `<` in a JSON script is written `\u003c`, so a value holding `</script>` cannot end it. `seo.jsonLd` takes the same data.
- Without `site` and `seo`, a page's head holds only the tags it and its layouts set.

### Sitemap and robots.txt

A project with a `site` serves `/sitemap.xml` and `/robots.txt`, which allows every crawler and points at the sitemap; a file of the same name in `public/` replaces either. The sitemap lists:

- every page without params, unless its server fence has `export const sitemap = false`;
- for a page with params, the ones its `sitemap` export lists, else the ones its `prerender` export lists, else none. `sitemap` takes what `prerender` takes: `true`, `false`, a content collection, a list of params or a function returning one;
- a page behind a guard only when its `sitemap` export lists it.

```kay
--- server
import { findPost, listPosts } from '../../data'

export async function sitemap() {
  return (await listPosts()).map(post => ({ slug: post.slug }))
}

const post = await findPost(ctx.params.slug) ?? ctx.notFound()
---
h1 {post.title}
```

In production the sitemap is built on the first request and kept for an hour; development builds it per request.

### Favicon and web manifest

`favicon` in `kay.config.ts` names a square image, 512 pixels wide or more, relative to the root: `favicon: 'src/favicon.png'`. kay serves it as `/favicon.ico` (16, 32 and 48 pixels), `/apple-touch-icon.png` (180), `/icon-192.png` and `/icon-512.png`, plus `/manifest.webmanifest`, and links them from every page. `kay build` writes them; development makes them from the image on first request. Each path a public file or a page already serves is left to it.

```ts
import { defineConfig } from 'kay/server'

export default defineConfig({
  favicon: 'src/favicon.png',
  seo: { name: 'Example' },
  manifest: { shortName: 'Ex', themeColor: '#1e1e2e', backgroundColor: '#11111b', display: 'standalone' },
})
```

The manifest is named after `seo.name`, `shortName` defaulting to it; `themeColor` is also every page's `theme-color`.

### Fonts

`fonts` in `kay.config.ts` self-hosts font files: each is served as a content-named asset, declared by one `@font-face` stylesheet every page links, and preloaded unless `preload: false`.

```ts
import { defineConfig } from 'kay/server'

export default defineConfig({
  fonts: [
    { family: 'Inter', src: '@fontsource-variable/inter/files/inter-latin-wght-normal.woff2', weight: '100 900' },
    { family: 'Lora', src: 'src/fonts/lora-italic.woff2', style: 'italic', preload: false },
  ],
})
```

- `src` is a `.woff2`, `.woff`, `.ttf` or `.otf` file relative to the root, or a file of an installed package. `weight` defaults to 400, or takes a range for a variable font; `style` to `normal`; `display` to `swap`; `unicodeRange` is passed through.
- A stylesheet names the family as it would any other: `font-family: Inter, system-ui, sans-serif`. With Tailwind, `@theme { --font-sans: Inter, system-ui, sans-serif; }`.
- Preload only the faces the first screen shows: each preload is fetched with the page, used or not.

## Styles

A component script or any `.ts` module imports its stylesheet: `import './card.css'`. Each page links one stylesheet per layout, outermost first, then its own, holding the CSS of every component it renders, islands included. Bun bundles them: `@import`, nesting and relative `url()` assets work, and `url(/logo.png)` is left for a public file.

Tailwind runs as a build plugin. `bun add -d tailwindcss bun-plugin-tailwind`, then:

```ts
import tailwind from 'bun-plugin-tailwind'
import { defineConfig } from 'kay/server'

export default defineConfig({ plugins: [tailwind] })
```

`src/app.css`, imported by the root `_layout.kay`, points Tailwind at the classes kay collects from the `.class` shorthand, which it cannot read off `div.md:flex.w-1/2` itself:

```css
@import 'tailwindcss';
@source '../.kay/classes.txt';
```

## Public files

Files in `public/` (the `publicDir` option) are served at their path as they are: `public/robots.txt` at `/robots.txt`, `public/logo@2x.png` at `/logo@2x.png`. A `:`, `*` or `'` in a name is served percent-encoded only, as `%3A`, `%2A` or `%27`. A file sharing its path with a page stops the server at boot, as do two pages serving one path.

## Imported files

A component script, a server fence or a `.ts` module imports an image, font, video, audio file or PDF for its URL, typed as a `string`:

```kay
---
import logo from '../logo.png'
---
img(src={logo} alt="Logo")
```

The URL, such as `/_kay/assets/logo-2k1v9.png`, is named after the file's content and served with a year of immutable caching, so a changed file gets a new URL; the server and islands render the same one, and `kay build` writes every file the pages import, through their modules and server fences too. A file to serve at a fixed path, such as `robots.txt`, goes in `public/` instead. The extension may be upper case, `logo.PNG`; `kay check` types the lower and upper case spellings only. These imports are kay's own: a build plugin of the project for the same extensions, such as one inlining SVG, does not apply to them.

### Responsive images

`image()` from `kay/image` gives an `img` the props that load the right size, spread into it:

```kay
---
import { image } from 'kay/image'
import hero from '../hero.jpg'
---
img({...image(hero, { sizes: '(min-width: 60rem) 50vw, 100vw' })} alt="The workshop")
```

- An imported PNG, JPEG or WebP gets a `srcset` of WebP variants at 320, 640, 960, 1280, 1920, 2560 and 3840 pixels wide, those below its own width, plus its own; `src` is the 1280 one, or the widest below it; `width` and `height` are its own, so the page keeps its space while it loads. `sizes` is passed through. Any other file, an SVG for instance, gets its `src` alone, with its size when kay read one.
- Variants are served by `/_kay/image?src=...&w=...`, which answers only those widths. `kay build` writes every variant of every imported image, served as files with a year of immutable caching; development makes them on request, kept in `.kay/cache/images`.
- Images added at runtime, such as uploads, are resized too from a directory listed by the URL path the app serves it at: `images: { dirs: { '/uploads/': 'data/uploads' } }` in `kay.config.ts`, relative to the root, or to where an executable runs. Give their size, `image(post.photo, { width: post.photoWidth, height: post.photoHeight })`, for the variants; without it the image keeps its `src` alone. Each variant is made once per version of the file and revalidated by its ETag, since an upload can change in place; one over 50 megapixels is refused with 413 from its header alone. kay does not serve the originals: the app does.
- `images.quality` sets the WebP quality, 80 by default. Variants are WebP, which every current browser reads; AVIF encoding is not available on Linux.
- An element with a spread is not checked for `alt`, so write it.

### Icons

Any [Iconify](https://icon-sets.iconify.design) set the project depends on as `@iconify-json/<prefix>` is imported one icon at a time, `~icons/<prefix>/<name>`, and drawn by spreading it into an `svg`:

```kay
---
import home from '~icons/tabler/home'
---
a(href="/")
  svg({...home} class="size-5")
  | Home
```

- The import gives the `viewBox`, the markup inlined as `innerHTML`, `aria-hidden="true"`, and a height of `1em` with the width of the icon's ratio, so it sizes to the text around it and takes its colour from `currentColor`; a class or style sizes it otherwise. An icon that means something on its own, with no text beside it, takes `role="img"` and an `aria-label`.
- Only the icons a page or an island imports are in the build; an alias renders as the icon it points at.
- `kay check` declares every icon of the installed sets in `.kay/types/kay-icons.d.ts`, so a misspelt name is reported as a module it cannot find; a bundle naming one fails with the set and the name. kay reads `@iconify-json/<prefix>` packages, not the all-in-one `@iconify/json`: each icon of an installed set is one declaration there and one virtual module the server registers at boot (Tabler, 6,400 icons, takes about 10 ms).

## Islands

A component is interactive when any element in it has an `on*` handler, a `bind:` or a `ref`, or when its script imports a value from `kay`, such as `signal`. An interactive component renders on the server and hydrates in the browser as an island; everything else ships no JavaScript, except the small script swapping pages in on a page posting a form to an action (see Navigation). Interactive components rendered inside an island are part of it.

Props a static component passes to an island are serialized for the browser: plain objects and arrays, strings, numbers, booleans, `null` and `undefined`, and also Dates, Maps, Sets, bigints, URLs and RegExps, which arrive as themselves, a value referenced twice arriving once. `kay check` rejects functions and class instances there, and rendering throws on a class instance it could not tell apart, naming the prop. Children cannot cross either: rendering an island with children from a static parent throws.

An island hydrates as soon as the page loads, its chunks preloaded. `hydrate="idle"` waits until the browser is idle and `hydrate="visible"` until it scrolls near the viewport, neither preloaded: `Comments(postId={post.id} hydrate="visible")`. Only an island takes `hydrate`, and only from a static parent.

### Shared and persisted state

A signal a `.ts` module exports is one state for every island of the page that imports it: `export const cart = signal<Item[]>([])` in `src/cart.ts`, read by a header badge and written by a product's button.

- On the server a module outlives the request, so a value a page's, a layout's or an island's script writes to such a signal while the page renders, as `cart.set(items)` seeding it from props, holds for that request only, and everything rendered after it reads it. A module's `memo` is computed afresh on each read there.
- `signal('light', { persist: 'theme' })` keeps its value across pages and visits in a cookie named `theme`, which the server reads too, so a page rendered for the request shows the kept value from the first paint, and answers with `Vary: Cookie`. A page `kay build` prerendered renders the default, and the island corrects it as it hydrates. The cookie is named after `persist` as it is, so it never reuses the name of a cookie the app sets itself.
- `{ persist: 'draft', storage: 'local' }` keeps it in localStorage instead, which the server never sees: the page renders the default and the kept value applies once the islands reading it have hydrated, so it suits what the first paint does not show.
- A persisted value crosses as island props do, Dates, Maps and Sets included. A cookie value over about 3.8 KB encoded is not kept, with a warning; one written by another version of the app, or by hand, that does not decode leaves the default. A value that decodes is not checked against the signal's type, so one whose shape the code relies on is checked before use. The cookie is `SameSite=Lax`, for the site's mount point, kept a year, and `Secure` over https.

### Error fallbacks

A `try` block renders its `catch` block instead when what it renders throws, so one broken widget does not take the page down:

```kay
try
  Chart(points={points})
catch error
  p.error The chart could not be drawn: {(error as Error).message}
```

- It works in any template. On the server, a block that throws renders `catch`, and the error goes to the log and `onError` like any render error, the page answering 200. Without `try`, a render error fails the page as before.
- In an island, a block that throws while it hydrates, or later as a signal it reads changes, renders `catch` in its place, its effects disposed. The error is logged and sent to the server, where `onError` gets it as a `BrowserError` from `kay/server`, with `kind`, the error's own name such as `TypeError`, `message`, `stack`, the page's `url`, its path without query or hash, and `island`, the island's component path, when known. A block the server rendered `catch` for keeps that markup as it came, since the error stayed on the server.
- `catch` takes the error under a name or none, typed `unknown`. A `try` without `catch` renders nothing when it throws.
- An error no `try` catches in the browser, from an effect, a handler or a promise nobody awaited, is reported the same way; an island whose script throws as it hydrates keeps its server markup, lifeless. The browser sends at most 10 distinct errors per page load, leaving out another origin's scripts, whose details it hides, and the server takes 20 reports a minute per client, refusing another site's and any over 16 KB.

### Context

`context(defaultValue)` makes a value a component hands everything it renders, however deep, without passing it through each one's props:

```ts
// src/theme.ts
import { context } from 'kay'

export const Theme = context<'light' | 'dark'>('light')
```

A component's script calls `Theme.provide('dark')`, and any component it renders, its children and their blocks included, reads `Theme.use()`; a component beside it, or above, reads the nearest value provided above itself, else the default. Provide a signal to share a value that changes. `use()` reads while a component renders: a handler or a timer calls it with nothing above, getting the default, so the script reads it once and keeps it. A layout's provide reaches its page. An island reads nothing the page's static components provide, in the browser as on the server, since it hydrates on its own: provide inside the island.

### Unique ids

`uid()` from `kay` gives a component an id unique on the page, for tying a label to its control or a trigger to its popup, with no `id` prop to pass:

```kay
---
import { signal, uid } from 'kay'

const id = uid()
const open = signal(false)
---
button(aria-controls={id} aria-expanded={open() ? 'true' : 'false'} onClick={() => open.set(o => !o)}) Menu
ul(id={id} hidden={!open()})
  slot
```

- One per call, made once per component instance as its script runs, rows of a `for` included. An island draws the same ids in the browser as the server wrote, so `for`, `aria-controls` and `id` match once it hydrates.
- Importing `uid` alone keeps a component static; the ids of a page differ from one render to the next, so a test reads them off the markup rather than writing them, and a prerendered page that revalidates gets a new ETag each time.
- A `try` whose block fails on the server draws its `catch` block's ids apart, so the ids after it match the browser's, which keeps the server's markup there.

### Browser-only components

Some components cannot render on the server: a package that touches `window` as it loads, such as CodeMirror or hls.js, or code reading `localStorage` while rendering. Such a component renders in the browser only: the server sends its island as an empty `<slot>`, props included, and the browser renders it there as soon as the page loads, instead of hydrating it. Inside another island it renders nothing on the server and is built in place as its parent hydrates.

- An island importing a package that throws on a browser-only global as it loads renders in the browser only, with nothing to write. Each package is imported once, in a Bun process of its own, and the answer is kept per package version in `.kay/cache`. The server never loads the package: an island's server module carries none of its script.
- A component whose script fence is `--- client` always renders in the browser only, and is an island even without state. Pages, layouts and special pages render on the server, so they cannot be.
- `hydrate="client"` renders one use of an island in the browser only: `Map(center={center} hydrate="client")`.

A browser-only global is one lib.dom declares and Bun lacks: `window`, `document`, `localStorage`, `sessionStorage`, `innerWidth` and the like. `fetch`, `URL`, `WebSocket`, `crypto` and `navigator` exist on the server too and are never reported. `kay check` and the editor report one read while the component renders: at the script's top level, in a `memo` or an array callback such as `.map`, in a function of the script the render calls, or in a template value. Handlers, refs, `effect`, `onMount` and other callbacks run in the browser only and report nothing. The editor offers two fixes: wrap the statement in `effect`, offered for a statement that is a plain call or assignment, since a declaration would take its name out of reach, or turn the fence into `--- client`. `typeof window` while an island renders is reported too: it is `'undefined'` on the server, so the island would render something else in the browser than the markup it hydrates. A global reached through a module of the app or a package is not seen; in development, a server render failing on one names it, the `.kay` line reading it, and the same two fixes.

## Navigation

A page shipping kay's script, one with an island or a form posting to an action, swaps the next page in place: a link to another page of the app fetches it and puts its body and head in this one, without a reload, and the islands of the new page hydrate. Without JavaScript, or before the script loads, links and forms load pages as they always did.

- An island marked `persist` lives on from page to page, its state and its element kept, when the next page renders it too: `Player(persist)` in a layout keeps a song playing. A bare `persist` matches the same component on the next page; `persist="left"` names one use, for two uses of a component to be told apart. Only an island takes `persist`, and only from a static parent.
- A form posting to an action posts without a reload, then shows the page the post leads to, as the browser would: `ctx.failed` and `ctx.succeeded` read as after a full post, and a post going back to the same page keeps the scroll position and the focused field. While it posts, the form has `aria-busy="true"` and a second submit does nothing; a file upload's progress, from 0 to 1, is the form's `--kay-progress` custom property and the value of each `progress` inside it.
- Before posting, the browser checks the form against the action's schema, with the message the server would give, the schema's `error` option when set: the length, pattern, `email` and `uuid` formats and bounds of each field, numbers, booleans and list sizes. A refused field shows the browser's own bubble, cleared as it is edited. Files, hidden fields, missing required fields and the forms of an `await` block are left to the server, and a button with `formnovalidate` skips the check.
- `navigate('/todos/1')`, imported from `kay`, goes to a page as a link would, `{ replace: true }` taking the current history entry's place; another site's page loads. `refresh()` runs the current page's loads again and shows what they return, keeping the scroll, the focus and every island whose props did not change: an island calls it once an action changed what the page shows. Both do nothing on the server.
- A link or a form with `data-reload`, or inside an element with it, loads the next page fully; so do a link with `target` or `download`, one to another site, `/api` and `/_kay` paths, and modified clicks. A page in another locale, or one built against another client build, loads fully too.
- The swap moves focus to the new page's `autofocus` element, else its `h1`, and announces its title to screen readers. Going back or forward, or reloading, restores where each page was scrolled to, and a link to `#section` scrolls there. A page streaming `await` blocks is swapped in once they all arrived. `aria-busy="true"` sits on `html` while a page loads.
- The swap prefetches as the speculation rules would, `prefetch` setting when (see Project setup), and replaces them, so each page is fetched once: a hovered link's page is kept for 30 seconds and taken as the link is followed. `data-no-prefetch` still opts a link out.
- A stylesheet holding `@view-transition { navigation: auto; }` animates the swap where the browser has view transitions, as it animates full loads.
- `navigation: false` in `kay.config.ts` or `pages()` turns it off: pages load fully, and only pages with islands ship a script.

## Component libraries

A package can ship `.kay` components, which the app installing it compiles as its own: on the server, in islands, and in `kay build --compile` and `--static`.

Publishing one:

- Ship the `.kay` sources, list `kay` under `peerDependencies`, and import from `kay`, so the app's one copy of kay, and its registered types, serve the library too.
- Give each component a specifier in the exports map, `"exports": { "./*.kay": "./src/*.kay", ".": "./src/index.ts" }`, imported as `import Button from '@kaynooo/kayjs-ui/button.kay'`. Without an exports map a component is imported by its path in the package.
- Settings the app may replace, such as theme classes or an icon resolver, live in one module named in package.json, `"kay": { "settings": "./src/settings.ts" }`, which default-exports the settings and which the library's components import. Define the defaults in a module of their own, `./src/defaults.ts`, re-exported by the settings module, `export { default } from './defaults'`, and export the `Settings` type and the defaults from there for apps to extend: the app's module takes the place of the settings module, so anything read through it is the app's.

Using one:

- Install it and import its components; `kay check`, the editor, auto-import and go-to-definition included, types them through `.kay/types/kay-packages.d.ts`, and needs no change to `tsconfig.json`.
- Only the components the app's imports reach ship: an island of the library the app never imports adds nothing to its bundles, unless a module re-exporting every component, such as a barrel `index.ts`, is imported.
- The classes in their templates and in the library scripts they import, default theme classes included, reach `.kay/classes.txt` with the app's own, so Tailwind builds them with no `@source` line into `node_modules`.
- `kay check` reports a type error inside a library component the app uses once, at the component's own line; one the app never imports reports nothing.
- `settings` in `kay.config.ts` replaces a library's settings module with the app's, by the library's name, on the server and in the browser: `settings: { '@kaynooo/kayjs-ui': './src/ui-settings.ts' }`, a module default-exporting the library's `Settings`, which may spread the library's defaults to change a few: `export default { ...defaults, tone: 'text-red-500' }`. `kay check` checks it against the defaults it replaces. One process renders with one set of settings: `kay test`, the server and `kay build` all read them from `kay.config.ts`.
- A library linked rather than installed, `"@kaynooo/kayjs-ui": "link:../kayjs-ui"`, works the same.

## Pages and routing

Pages live in `src/routes/`:

| File | URL |
| --- | --- |
| `index.kay` | `/` |
| `about.kay` | `/about` |
| `todos/[id].kay` | `/todos/:id`, read as `ctx.params.id` |
| `docs/[...path].kay` | `/docs/*`, read as `ctx.params.path` |
| `blog/[[page]].kay` | `/blog` and `/blog/:page`, `ctx.params.page` a `string \| undefined` |
| `items/[id=integer].kay` | `/items/:id` where the matcher `integer` takes the segment, `ctx.params.id` the `number` it returns |
| `(marketing)/pricing.kay` | `/pricing`: a group, in parentheses, adds nothing to the URL, only its `_layout.kay` and `_guard.ts` |
| `_layout.kay` | Wraps every page in its directory and below, outermost first, rendering the page at its `slot`. |
| `_404.kay` | Rendered with status 404 for `ctx.notFound()` in its directory and below; the root one also answers URLs no page serves. |
| `_error.kay` | Rendered with status 500 when a load or render throws, and for 404s with no `_404.kay`. |
| `_guard.ts` | Runs before every page and every action in its directory and below; see Guards. |

A page URL ending in a slash redirects with 308 to the one without, query kept: `/about/` to `/about`. `trailingSlash` in kay.config.ts changes that: `'always'` redirects `/about` to `/about/` instead, `'ignore'` serves both.

A matcher checks a param, `[name=matcher]` or `[[name=matcher]]`: it returns the value `ctx.params` hands the page, typed as it returns it, or `undefined` to refuse the URL. kay ships `integer` (a safe whole number, as a number), `uuid` (lowercased) and `slug` (lowercase words joined by dashes), in `kay/params`; a project adds its own as `src/params/<name>.ts`, beside `src/routes/`, its default export the matcher, and one of that name wins over kay's. A matcher nobody provides stops the server.

```ts
// src/params/even.ts
export default (value: string) => Number(value) % 2 === 0 ? Number(value) : undefined
```

A URL a matcher refuses falls through to the page without one serving the same path, `items/[slug].kay` beside `items/[id=integer].kay`, and is a 404 when none does; several pages with matchers on one path are tried in the order of their file paths. Two pages serving one path, neither with a matcher, stop the server, whatever they name their params: `todos/[id].kay` and `todos/[slug].kay`, `blog/index.kay` and `blog/[[page]].kay`, `about.kay` and `(site)/about.kay`. A `prerender` list leaves an optional param out to prerender the path without it, and an entry a matcher refuses fails the build.

A page or a layout whose server fence has a line starting with `export const layouts = false` is wrapped by none of the layouts above it: `export const layouts = false` gives a page none at all, a layout starts the chain afresh, so a section can drop the site's header.

Other files starting with `_` are not routes. Every top-level name the server fence declares reaches the template, typed. The fence runs per request and may use top-level `await` and the `ctx` object, except what an export such as an action reads: that runs once, when the module loads, so it may neither await nor read `ctx`, which `kay check` reports. The fence's `ctx`:

- `ctx.params`, typed from the file name, `ctx.url`, `ctx.request`
- `ctx.query`, the search params, read against the schema the page exports as `query`: `export const query = t.Object({ q: t.String(), page: t.Optional(t.Integer()) })` types `ctx.query.page` as a `number | undefined`. Each is read as a form field is (a number from decimal text, a list from a repeated name, `true` from `on`), one left out takes its `default`, and a query the schema refuses renders `_error.kay` with status 400, once the guards let the request through. Layouts read the page's, and declare none of their own; `query` is no action name for that reason. Without a schema each name reads as its text, a repeated one as a list, typed `unknown`; the raw text is `ctx.url.searchParams`.
- `ctx.cookies`, a `Bun.CookieMap`: `ctx.cookies.get('theme')`; what `set` and `delete` change is sent back, redirects included
- `ctx.locals`, what the app's Elysia `derive`, `resolve` and `decorate` add, such as the signed-in user
- `ctx.status(404)` and `ctx.headers` set the response
- `ctx.redirect('/login')`, `ctx.notFound()` and `ctx.deny(403, 'Members only')` stop rendering; `deny` renders `_error.kay` with that status and message

Layout and page loads run in parallel; when several fail, the outermost one decides the response. In development each response carries a `Server-Timing` header with the time of every load and of the render, shown in the browser's network panel.

The nearest special page wins, wrapped by the layouts of its own directory. `_error.kay` reads `ctx.error`: `status`, `message` and, in development only, `stack`. Logged and displayed stacks point at `.kay` lines. In production the message is generic and the real error goes to `console.error`; without an `_error.kay` the response is plain text, and development shows the stack instead.

```kay
--- server
const { status, message } = ctx.error
---
h1 Error {status}
p {message}
```

```kay
--- server
import { findTodo } from '../../data'

const id = Number(ctx.params.id)
const todo = await findTodo(id) ?? ctx.notFound()
---
h1 {todo.title}
p.status {todo.done ? 'Done' : 'Open'}
```

Each error kay logs while answering a request, from a load, a render, a guard, an action, a streamed block without `catch` or a `try` block's, also goes to the `onError` option of `kay.config.ts` or `pages()`, the place to send it to an error tracker. The response does not wait for a promise it returns, and an error it throws is logged:

```ts
import { defineConfig } from 'kay/server'

export default defineConfig({
  onError: (error, request) => tracker.capture(error, { url: request.url }),
})
```

## Prerendering

A page whose server fence has `export const prerender = true` is rendered once by `kay build`, its loads included, and served from that file in production, revalidated by its ETag. Its guards still run on every request. It renders without a request, so reading `ctx.cookies`, `ctx.query`, `ctx.locals`, `ctx.failed` or `ctx.succeeded` fails the build; `ctx.url` is `http://localhost` plus its path. Development renders it per request like any other.

A route taking params lists the ones to render instead, as an array or a function returning one; any other path renders per request:

```kay
--- server
import { findPost, listPosts } from '../../data'

export async function prerender() {
  return (await listPosts()).map(post => ({ slug: post.slug }))
}

const post = await findPost(ctx.params.slug) ?? ctx.notFound()
---
h1 {post.title}
```

Each value is a string with no empty, `.` or `..` segment, a catch-all's included with its slashes. `export const prerender = false` prerenders nothing.

`export const revalidate = 3600` beside `prerender` keeps a prerendered page fresh: once it is older than that many seconds, the next request still gets it as it is, and starts rendering it again in the background, the way `kay build` does; every request after that render lands gets the new page, with a new ETag and compressed copies. One render runs at a time per path. A render that fails or answers 5xx is logged and leaves the page as it was, the next attempt coming a minute later at most. The new page lives in memory, so a restart serves the built file again until it goes stale; an executable built a while ago revalidates on its first request.

## Content collections

A collection is a folder of Markdown files, or of JSON and YAML data files, read against a schema. The project declares its collections in `src/content.config.ts`, or the module `content` names in kay.config.ts, each folder relative to that module:

```ts
import { t } from 'elysia'
import { collection } from 'kay/content'
import Callout from './components/callout.kay'

export const posts = collection('content/posts', {
  schema: t.Object({ title: t.String(), date: t.Date(), tags: t.Array(t.String(), { default: [] }), draft: t.Optional(t.Boolean()) }),
  components: { Callout },
  draft: post => post.data.draft === true,
  sort: (a, b) => b.data.date.getTime() - a.data.date.getTime(),
  feed: { path: '/blog/rss.xml', title: 'Blog', item: post => ({ title: post.data.title, path: `/blog/${post.slug}`, date: post.data.date }) },
})

export const authors = collection('content/authors', { schema: t.Object({ name: t.String() }) })
```

A page reads it in its server fence, typed from the schema:

```kay
--- server
import { posts } from '../../content.config'

export const prerender = posts

const post = await posts.get(ctx.params.slug) ?? ctx.notFound()
const { Content } = post
---
h1 {post.data.title}
nav
  for heading of post.headings key={heading.id}
    a(href={`#${heading.id}`}) {heading.text}
article
  Content
```

- `all()` gives every entry in the collection's `sort` order, by slug without one; filter and sort it like any array. `get(slug)` gives one entry or `undefined`. An entry `draft` returns true for shows in `kay dev` only: everywhere else it is left out of `all()`, `get()`, prerendering, the sitemap and the feed. Two files giving one slug, `guides.md` and `guides/index.md`, fail the collection.
- An entry has `slug`, its path in the folder without the extension (`guides/intro`; an `index` file takes its folder's), `data`, `headings` (`{ depth, id, text }` in order, for a table of contents), `Content`, the component rendering its body, and `file`. A data file's `headings` is empty and its `Content` renders nothing.
- A Markdown file starts with YAML frontmatter between `---` lines. Every entry's data is read against the schema: defaults filled in, a `t.Date()` decoded from its text. An entry it refuses, or one that does not parse, fails `kay check` at the field's line, and fails `kay build` and the first load.
- Headings get ids, deduplicated, and link to themselves. Bare URLs become links.
- `highlight: (code, language) => html` highlights code blocks as entries compile, at build time: it returns the whole `<pre>`, such as Shiki's `codeToHtml`, which the site depends on itself. Without one, a block renders as `<pre><code class="language-ts">`.
- A Markdown entry uses the components its collection's `components` names, written with a capital as in a template: `<Callout type="warn">` on its own line, Markdown inside after a blank line, then `</Callout>` on its own line; `<Badge text="new" />` inline. Attributes are text (`type="warn"`), JSON in braces (`count={3}`, `items={["a", "b"]}`), or bare for `true`, and may spread over several lines. An interactive component renders as an island and hydrates as in any page. A tag in a code span, a fenced code block or an indented one stays text. A component the collection does not name, or a tag left open, fails `kay check` and the build.
- `export const prerender = posts` in a page with one param prerenders a page per entry, its slug as the param; `sitemap` takes a collection the same way. A slug with a slash needs a catch-all page, `[...slug].kay`.
- Entries are the site's own content, trusted: their HTML, links and what a highlighter returns go out as written, unsanitised.
- `feed` serves an RSS 2.0 feed at its path, `format: 'atom'` for Atom, its `author` the feed's title unless set: the newest `limit` items, 20 by default, that `item` returns, links absolute on the `site` kay.config.ts sets, which a feed needs.
- Each entry compiles once and is cached in `.kay/cache/content` by its content, the highlighter's source and Bun's version, so a change, which restarts `kay dev`, recompiles that entry only. A highlighter whose output changes with no change to its source, such as a new theme passed in, needs that folder cleared. `kay build` compiles every collection into `.kay/client/content`, which production reads, an executable included, instead of the files.

## Locales

`i18n` in kay.config.ts serves every page in each locale, the default one unprefixed and the others under their prefix: `/about` and `/en/about`.

```ts
export default defineConfig({
  i18n: { locales: ['fr', 'en'], defaultLocale: 'fr' },
})
```

- `prefixDefault: true` puts the default locale under its prefix too, `/fr/about`; a path without one then redirects with a 307 to the visitor's locale: the one they last went to, kept in the `kay-locale` cookie once they follow a link of the site to it, then the best match of their browser's `Accept-Language`, then the default. Without it the URL alone decides.
- `domains: { fr: 'example.fr', en: 'example.com' }` serves each locale on its own host instead, with no prefixes; a host not listed serves the default locale, and every locale needs a host.
- A page cannot sit under a locale's prefix itself, `src/routes/en/`: kay serves every page there already. A root `[slug].kay` with no `index.kay` would take `/en` as a slug, so give the site an index page.
- `domains` and `prefixDefault` do not go together.

Messages live in `src/messages/<locale>.ts`, one file per locale, `messages` in `i18n` naming another directory. Each exports its messages by default through `defineMessages`, nested as you like, a group never holding only keys named like plural forms (`one`, `other`...), which would read as one plural message; the default locale's file is the reference `kay check` holds the others to, and a key a locale lacks falls back to the default locale's text.

```ts
import { defineMessages } from 'kay/i18n'

export default defineMessages({
  nav: { home: 'Accueil' },
  greeting: 'Bonjour {name}',
  items: { zero: 'Aucun article', one: '{count} article', other: '{count} articles' },
})
```

`kay/i18n` works anywhere a request is served from: loads, templates, components, islands, actions and guards.

- `t('greeting', { name })` gives a message in the request's locale, its key and placeholders typed from the default locale's file. A number fills a placeholder formatted for the locale, `1 234` in French, and a date with `dateStyle: 'medium'`. An object of plural forms is picked by `count` through `Intl.PluralRules`, `zero` taking 0 whenever it is given. A key no locale has renders as itself.
- `formatNumber(value, options)` and `formatDate(value, options)` format through `Intl` for the request's locale; `locale()` names it, as do `ctx.locale` in pages and guards and an action's `ctx.locale`.
- `localize('/about')` is that path in the request's locale, or in the one given as second argument, checked like any link; `alternate('en')` is the page being rendered in another locale, for a language switcher. With domains, a locale on another host gives its absolute URL.
- An island gets only the messages it uses: those it looks up while rendering on the server and the keys its own source passes `t()` as they are written. A key built at runtime, or looked up only in a module the island imports, reaches the browser only if the server render used it.
- An action runs in the locale of the page it was sent from, read off its `Referer`, then the cookie and the browser's languages.

The page's `<html lang>` is its locale. With `site`, every page links its copy in each locale, `<link rel="alternate" hreflang>`, `x-default` being the default locale's, its canonical URL is its own locale's, and the sitemap lists every copy with the others as `xhtml:link` alternates. `kay build` prerenders a page once per locale.

## Caching

`cached(key, ttl, load)` from `kay/cache` keeps what a load fetches for `ttl` seconds, shared by every request in the process:

```kay
--- server
import { cached } from 'kay/cache'
import { listPosts } from '../data'

const posts = await cached('posts', 300, listPosts)
---
```

- Concurrent calls for a key missing from the cache share one `load`.
- Past `ttl`, the next call still gets the stale value and refreshes it in the background, so no request waits on a refresh.
- A first load that throws throws to its callers and keeps nothing. A refresh that throws is logged and keeps the stale value, trying again a minute later at most.
- `invalidate(key)`, or `invalidate(key => key.startsWith('post:'))`, drops keys so the next call loads afresh: call it from the action that changed what they hold. A load already running for a dropped key never lands in the cache.
- The value is the same object for every caller, so it is never mutated. At most 10,000 keys are kept, the least recently written going first.
- The cache lives in the process: each server process keeps its own, and `kay dev` empties it on every change.

## Streaming

A load waits for every `await` in its server fence before the page renders. A value the page can show later is made with `defer()` instead, left unawaited, and rendered by an `await` block:

```kay
--- server
import { defer } from 'kay'
import { findPost, listComments } from '../../data'

const post = await findPost(Number(ctx.params.id)) ?? ctx.notFound()
const comments = defer(listComments(post.id))
---
h1 {post.title}
await comments
  p Loading comments
then list
  ul
    for comment of list key={comment.id}
      li {comment.body}
catch
  p Comments are unavailable
```

- The page goes out at once with the block under `await`. Each `then` block streams in as its value resolves, in whatever order they do, swapped in by a few bytes of inline script; islands inside it hydrate when it lands.
- `await value then name` on one line has no pending block. `catch error` binds the rejection; without `catch`, a rejection removes the pending block and is logged. A `then` block that throws while rendering is a bug, not a rejection: it removes the pending block and is logged too, never showing `catch`.
- `defer()` handles a rejection where the promise is made. Without it, a promise rejecting before the page renders it would crash the server, so `kay check` refuses a bare promise in `await`.
- Status, headers and cookies are sent before the first block, so a streamed block cannot redirect or set them, and a `head` block inside one is ignored. A block renders on its own, outside its layouts, and an `await` inside a pending block renders its own pending block only.
- The response stays open until the last value settles. Bun closes a connection idle for `idleTimeout` seconds, 10 by default, so a value slower than that needs `Bun.serve({ idleTimeout })` raised.
- In an island, the server sends the pending block and the browser renders the rest once the value settles.

## Actions

A page's or a layout's server fence exports actions: an Elysia schema and a handler. Each one becomes `POST /_kay/action/<file>/<name>`, with its input validated.

```kay
--- server
import { t } from 'elysia'
import { action } from 'kay'
import { addTodo, listTodos } from '../data'

export const add = action(t.Object({ title: t.String({ minLength: 1, error: 'Write a title' }) }), async ({ title }, ctx) => {
  if ((await listTodos()).some(todo => todo.title === title))
    return ctx.fail(409, { message: 'Already on the list' })

  return (await addTodo(title)).id
})

const todos = await listTodos()
const failure = ctx.failed(add)
---
ul
  for todo of todos key={todo.id}
    li: a(href={`/todos/${todo.id}`}) {todo.title}
form(action={add})
  input(name="title" placeholder="New todo" value={failure?.values.title})
  if failure?.errors.title as message
    p.error {message}
  if failure?.data as data
    p.error {data.message}
  button Add
```

- `form(action={add})` posts without JavaScript; `kay check` verifies every field `name` against the schema. After the post the browser goes back to the page, or wherever the handler's `ctx.redirect` points.
- A plain form posts text, read against the schema before it validates: a `t.Number()`, `t.Integer()` or `t.Boolean()` field becomes one, a number only from decimal text such as `-1.5` or `2e3`, never `0x10` (a ticked checkbox posts `on`, read as `true`, and an unticked one nothing, read as `false` when the field is required), a `t.Array()` field takes a single value or none as a list, and a blank optional field other than a plain `t.String()` counts as left out.
- A post the schema refuses, or whose handler returns `ctx.fail(status, data)`, goes back to the page too. There `ctx.failed(add)` returns `{ status, values, errors, data }`, typed from the action, or `undefined`: `values` is what the form posted (fields named like a password left out), `errors` a message per refused field, the schema's `error` option when set, and `data` what `ctx.fail` received. It is read on that one render only.
- A post that succeeds goes back to the page with what the handler returned: `ctx.succeeded(add)` returns `{ data }`, typed from the action, or `undefined`, on that one render only. `data` and `ctx.fail`'s data travel in a cookie, so one too big for it, over about 3.5 KB encoded, is left out with a warning, and `ctx.succeeded` returns `undefined`. A forged cookie only changes what its own sender sees.
- An island imports the action from the page and calls it: `import { add } from '../routes/index.kay'`, then `const id = await add({ title })`, and `add.pending()` reads, reactively, whether a call the page made is still in flight: `button(disabled={add.pending()})`. The call is typed, `ctx.fail` results excluded, and throws `ActionError` with `status`, `errors` and `data` when it fails. Its input, its result and that `data` cross as island props do, Dates, Maps, Sets and bigints included; a result holding a function or a class instance answers 500, logging where it sits. When the handler or a guard redirects, the browser goes there, swapping the page in as a link would, and the call never resolves; outside a browser, as in a test, it throws `ActionRedirect` with `location`.
- An island holding a form may call the action with its fields instead, `await add(new FormData(form))`: the server reads them as it reads a plain form post, numbers, booleans and arrays coerced from their text, a blank optional field other than a string left out, files and the honeypot included, and answers as a call, so the island shows the field errors of the `ActionError` and goes on once it resolves.
- Files: `t.File()` or `t.Files()` in the schema, `input(type="file" name="avatar")` in the form, and the handler gets a `File`. Forms posting to an action are sent as `multipart/form-data` unless they set `enctype`, and a file input left empty counts as no file, so `t.Optional(t.File())` works. An island passes a `File` or `Blob` anywhere in its input, nested ones included: `await upload({ avatar: input.files[0] })`. On a top-level field, `t.File({ type: 'image/png' })` checks the file's bytes, not its name or declared type, and a file it refuses fails like any field, under its name in `errors` with the schema's `error` option when set; a nested file is checked against the type it declares only. Bun caps a request body at 128 MB, changed with `new Elysia({ serve: { maxRequestBodySize } })`.
- A handler that throws answers 500 with a generic message and logs the error.
- The handler's second argument has `request`, `cookies`, `locals`, `status(code)`, `headers`, `redirect(location)` and `fail(status, data)`, whose status is an error status, 400 to 599. A location outside ASCII, such as `/blog/日本語`, goes out percent-encoded, from pages and guards too; one holding a control character, or a scheme other than `http:` and `https:`, such as `javascript:`, throws.
- A post another site sends, as its `Origin` or `Sec-Fetch-Site` header shows, is refused with 403. The cookie carrying `ctx.failed` and `ctx.succeeded` back is `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Lax`, and `Secure` when the request came over https, `X-Forwarded-Proto` included.
- A third argument protects an action from scripts: `action(schema, handler, { rateLimit: { max: 5, window: 60 }, honeypot: 'website' })`. `rateLimit` lets one client post `max` times every `window` seconds, then answers 429 with `Retry-After` and `errors['']` saying when to retry, counting every attempt, valid or not; the client is the request's address, or behind a proxy on the same machine or network the address it appended last to `X-Forwarded-For`. An IPv6 client counts as its /64 block, which one host or home network holds. Counts live in the process, so each server process keeps its own, for at most 10,000 clients per action, the oldest windows dropped past that. `honeypot` names a field the form renders out of sight, `input(name="website" tabindex="-1" autocomplete="off" aria-hidden="true")` hidden by a class, which people leave empty and bots fill in: a form post giving it any value, a file included, fails with 422 and `errors.website`, and `kay check` takes it as one of the form's fields. Neither reaches the handler.
- A library or route limiting attempts its own way reads the client as `rateLimit` does: `clientAddress(request, server)` from `kay/server` gives the address, a proxy's appended one included, and `rateKey(address)` the key a limit counts it under, an IPv6 address's /64 block.

## Locals

`ctx.locals` is the Elysia context of the request. Declare what the app adds once, in a `.ts` module, and register its type:

```ts
import type { LocalsOf } from 'kay'
import { Elysia } from 'elysia'

export const auth = new Elysia({ name: 'auth' }).derive({ as: 'scoped' }, async ({ cookie }) => ({ user: await findSession(cookie.session?.value) }))

declare module 'kay' {
  interface Register {
    locals: LocalsOf<typeof auth>
  }
}
```

## Sessions

`session()` from `kay/server` is an Elysia plugin adding `session` to the context: `ctx.locals.session` in pages, actions and guards, `({ session })` in the app's own Elysia routes.

```ts
import type { LocalsOf } from 'kay'
import { session, sqliteStore } from 'kay/server'
import { env } from './env'

export const sessions = session<{ userId: string }>({ secret: env.SESSION_SECRET, store: sqliteStore('sessions.sqlite') })

declare module 'kay' {
  interface Register {
    locals: LocalsOf<typeof sessions>
  }
}
```

The server entry uses it before the pages: `new Elysia().use(sessions).use(await pages())`. An app with locals of its own registers `LocalsOf` of an Elysia that uses both.

```kay
--- server
import { t } from 'elysia'
import { action } from 'kay'

export const signIn = action(t.Object({ email: t.String(), password: t.String() }), async (input, ctx) => {
  const user = await verify(input)

  if (!user)
    return ctx.fail(401, { message: 'Wrong email or password' })

  await ctx.locals.session.regenerate()
  await ctx.locals.session.set('userId', user.id)
  ctx.redirect('/')
})

const userId = await ctx.locals.session.get('userId')
---
```

- `get(key)`, `set(key, value)` and `unset(key)` are typed from the plugin's type parameter. `destroy()` forgets the session and clears its cookie, for signing out. `regenerate()` moves the data to a new id, for right after signing in, so an id planted before it is worth nothing. All of them return promises.
- `secret` is at least 32 characters, read from the environment. A list rotates secrets: the first seals new cookies, every one opens old ones, and a cookie an older one sealed goes out sealed with the first on its next use.
- Without a `store`, the data travels in the cookie, sealed with AES-GCM so it can be neither read nor altered, about 3.5 KB at most: past that the response fails with an error saying so. Such a cookie cannot be revoked: `destroy()` clears the browser's copy, but one taken before stays valid until `maxAge`, so a site that must end a session everywhere, after a password change say, uses a store. With a store, the cookie carries only a sealed id, and `destroy()` deletes the session itself. `memoryStore()` keeps sessions in the process, gone on restart. `sqliteStore(path)` keeps them in a SQLite file shared by the processes on one machine. Any object with `get(id)`, `set(id, data, maxAge)` and `delete(id)`, each sync or async, is a store too, such as one over Redis.
- Values cross as island props do, Dates, Maps, Sets and bigints included.
- The cookie, `session` unless `cookie` names another, is `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Lax`, `Path=/`, and `Secure` over https, `X-Forwarded-Proto` included. It is read on first use only, and written only when the session changed or is due an extension: a session lasts `maxAge` seconds without use, 30 days by default, and one used past half of it is extended. A forged or expired cookie reads as an empty session and is cleared.

## Environment

`defineEnv` from `kay/server` reads `process.env` once against a schema, as the server boots, and gives it back typed:

```ts
import { t } from 'elysia'
import { defineEnv } from 'kay/server'

export const env = defineEnv(t.Object({
  DATABASE_URL: t.String(),
  PORT: t.Integer({ default: 3000 }),
  DEBUG: t.Optional(t.Boolean()),
}))
```

A number or boolean is read from its text as a form field is, a variable left out takes its `default`, and any missing or refused stops the boot with an error naming each one. The object holds the declared names only. Server code imports it: a `.ts` module, a server fence, the server entry; an island never sees the server's environment.

## Guards

A `_guard.ts` in a routes directory runs before every page and every action in that directory and below, outermost first. It lets the request through unless it redirects or denies:

```ts
import { guard } from 'kay'

export default guard(({ locals, redirect, deny }) => {
  if (locals.user === undefined)
    redirect('/login')

  if (!locals.user.admin)
    deny(403, 'Admins only')
})
```

- Its `ctx` has `request`, `url`, `cookies`, `locals`, `headers`, `redirect` and `deny`; cookies and headers it sets reach the response either way.
- It decides from who is asking, never from the page's params: actions have none, and their `url` is the action's own. Checks on one record belong in the load and the action.
- An action's guards run once its input is valid, when the app's `resolve` values are there: input the schema refuses gets its field errors back without reaching a guard or the handler. A refused form post gets the redirect, or the denial as plain text.
- A denied page renders the nearest `_error.kay` outside the guard's directory, inside the layouts outside it, so nothing the guard protects renders.
- A layout's `ctx.redirect` is no guard: actions never run layout loads. Neither is an Elysia `onBeforeHandle` testing the page's path: actions are served under `/_kay/action/`.

## API routes

Each `.ts` module under `src/api/`, the `api` option of `kay.config.ts` naming another directory, exports an Elysia instance by default, which `pages()` mounts at `/api` plus its path there, with nothing to register: `src/api/chat.ts` serves its routes under `/api/chat`, `src/api/index.ts` under `/api`. Files and directories starting with `_`, and `.test.ts` files, are left out.

```ts
import { t } from 'elysia'
import { api, events } from 'kay/server'
import { complete, listRooms } from '../data'

export default api()
  .get('/rooms', () => listRooms())
  .ws('/:room', {
    body: t.Object({ text: t.String() }),
    response: t.Object({ from: t.String(), text: t.String() }),
    message(ws, { text }) {
      ws.send({ from: ws.data.user?.name ?? 'guest', text })
    },
  })
  .post('/answer', ({ body }) => events(complete(body.prompt)), { body: t.Object({ prompt: t.String() }) })
```

- `api()` is a `new Elysia()` whose handlers read the app's locals, typed through `Register`: `({ user })`, `ws.data.user`. A plain `new Elysia()` is mounted the same way.
- A `_guard.ts` in `src/api/` or below runs before every route of the modules in its directory and below, outermost first, a websocket upgrade included, as it does for pages and actions: a redirect or a denial answers the request, and the cookies and headers it sets go out with the route's response.
- A websocket upgrade, or a request other than GET, HEAD and OPTIONS, another site's page sends, as its `Origin` or `Sec-Fetch-Site` header shows, is refused with 403 once the guards let it through, since a browser lets any page open a websocket or post a form to any host with the user's cookies. A request carrying neither header, such as a webhook, goes through; a route other sites' pages call from the browser belongs on the app's own Elysia instance.
- `events(source)` answers with server-sent events, one per value an async iterable, a generator or an array gives, crossing as island props do, Dates, Maps and Sets included. The source is read once the browser reads the response and stopped when it goes away; a source that throws ends the stream as failed, the error logged and handed to `onError`. A comment line every 5 seconds keeps a quiet stream open past Bun's `idleTimeout` and a proxy's.
- `kay check` checks links and redirects against the modules' GET routes, `/api/chat/rooms` here; `kay build --compile` embeds the modules, and `kay build --static` refuses them.

An island imports a module for its routes:

```kay
---
import { signal, socket, stream } from 'kay'
import chat from '../api/chat'

const { room } = props<{ room: string }>()
const messages = socket(chat, '/:room', { params: { room } })
const text = signal('')
---
p {messages.status()}
p {messages.last()?.text}
input(bind:value={text})
button(onClick={() => messages.send({ text: text() })}) Send
```

- `socket(module, path, options)` opens one of the module's websocket routes, the path written as the module writes it, `params` and `query` filling it in, all typed from the route. `send` takes the route's `body`, `last()` reads the last message reactively, typed from its `response`, `on(listener)` gets each one and returns what stops it, and `status()` is `connecting`, `open` or `closed`. Messages travel as Elysia sends them, as JSON. What is sent before the connection opens goes once it does. A connection that drops reconnects, waiting longer each time up to 30 seconds, unless the server closed it with code 1000; `close()` closes it for good.
- `stream(module, path, options)` reads one of its routes answering with `events()`, with `last()`, `on()` and `status()` the same way, `status()` being `done` once the stream ran to its end and `failed` when a guard or the route refused it or its source threw. `{ method: 'post', body }` reads a route taking a body, such as an AI answer. A GET stream that drops reconnects; any other ends as failed.
- Both open once the island is in the page, never on the server, and close with the component that opened them. The browser build gives the island the module's mount and none of its code, so its other exports never reach the browser, and an island importing any other file under `src/api/`, such as a `_schemas.ts`, fails the build: code an island shares with a module lives outside it.
- A refused upgrade looks like a dropped connection to the browser, so a socket a guard refuses keeps retrying, `connecting`, every 30 seconds at most.

## Testing

`kay/test` serves the project's pages and actions inside the test process, with no server and, unless asked for, no browser build:

```ts
import { expect, it } from 'bun:test'
import { testSite } from 'kay/test'
import { add } from '../src/routes/index.kay'

const site = await testSite({ locals: () => ({ user: { id: 1, admin: true } }) })

it('shows why a todo was refused', async () => {
  const page = await site.submit(add, { title: '' }, { from: '/' })

  expect(page.html).toContain('Write a title')
})
```

- `site.visit(path)` GETs a page and follows redirects, stopping at one to another site. `site.submit(action, fields, { from })` posts a form without JavaScript, as multipart with any `File` among its fields, and follows it back to its page. Both resolve with `{ url, status, headers, html }`. `site.call(action, input)` calls an action as an island does, `input` its typed input or a `FormData`, resolving with its result, throwing `ActionError` when it fails and `ActionRedirect` with `location` when it redirects.
- `site.fetch(path, init)` sends any request, an API route's included, with the cookies so far, and resolves with the response as it is, redirects not followed.
- `site.socket(module, path, options)` opens a websocket route and `site.stream(module, path, options)` reads an event stream as an island does, the options taking `headers` too. Both keep every message in `received` and resolve `next()` with the oldest one not read yet, waiting for one if need be; a stream's `finished()` resolves with all its values once it ended. `site.socket` starts the site on a free port the first time, which `site.close()` stops.
- Cookies a response sets go with the next request and read as `site.cookies`. `use` takes the plugins the server entry uses before the pages, in order, so an app on `session()` signs in through `site.submit` and stays signed in: `testSite({ use: [sessions] })`. `locals` stands in for the app's Elysia `derive`, called with each request, after those plugins.
- `mount(file, props)` renders one component built for the browser, as an island renders, into `document`, and resolves with `{ root, unmount }` once its effects ran: for what handlers and effects do, such as a dialog opening on a click. `file` is the `.kay` file relative to the project, since importing it through the preload gives its server build; props may be functions, and the component runs on a kay of its own, so a signal of the test reaches it through a callback rather than as a prop; a library's settings apply as `kay.config.ts` sets them. The test registers the DOM itself, such as `GlobalRegistrator.register()` from `@happy-dom/global-registrator`. After an interaction, `await settle()` lets effects land before the DOM is read.
- Without `browser`, pages render their islands' markup without scripts. Test files import `.kay` files through `[test] preload = ["kay/test/preload"]` in `bunfig.toml`, which `kay new` writes along with a first test. The preload serves the project in the working directory, or the one `KAY_ROOT` names when it is nested, such as a library's fixture app run as `KAY_ROOT=tests/fixture bun test`, which `testSite()` then serves too.
- `testSite({ browser: true })` also builds the islands for the browser, into `.kay/client` as `kay dev` does, and `site.open(path)` loads a page in a headless Chrome over a server the site starts on a free port, resolving with a page once it loaded and its islands hydrating on load are done; `browse(url)` opens a server already running the same way. The page clicks as a user does, `click(selector)` waiting for the element to be visible, still and not covered, and `fill(selector, text)` replaces a field's text as typing does; `type(text)` and `press(key)` go to the focused element. `text`, `value` and `count` read the page at once, `text` and `value` null when nothing matches; `waitFor(selector, { text, gone })` and `waitUntil(fn)` poll until they hold, 5 seconds at most unless `timeout` says otherwise, and fail naming what they waited for. `evaluate(fn, ...args)` runs a function in the page, its arguments and result crossing as JSON. `goto`, `back`, `forward` and `reload` resolve once the page settled, a swapped page included, and `path()` reads where it is. `errors` holds the page's console errors and uncaught exceptions, and `view` the `Bun.WebView` behind it, for a `screenshot()` or a raw `cdp()` call. Each page opened starts with no cookie or storage for the site, and pages opened at once share them, the browser's own rather than `site.cookies`. `site.close()` closes the pages it opened.
- The browser is `Bun.WebView` on its Chrome backend, young in Bun and marked experimental, so kay keeps to the part of it these helpers use. It runs the executable given as `path`, to `testSite({ browser: { path } })` or `open`, else `BUN_CHROME_PATH`, else the first Chrome or Chromium on the `PATH` or where it usually installs; with none, `open` fails saying so, and `describe.skipIf(!browserPath())` skips a suite instead. In an Alpine CI image, `apk add chromium` and `BUN_CHROME_PATH=$(command -v chromium)`; as root, as in a container, Chrome runs without its sandbox.

```ts
import { afterAll, expect, it } from 'bun:test'
import { testSite } from 'kay/test'

const site = await testSite({ browser: true })

afterAll(async () => site.close())

it('counts the clicks', async () => {
  const page = await site.open('/')

  await page.click('button.counter')
  await page.waitFor('button.counter', { text: 'Clicked 1' })
  expect(page.errors).toEqual([])
})
```

## What `kay check` verifies

- Every expression, prop and server name, as TypeScript does.
- `a(href="/todos/1")` and template literals such as `` `/todos/${id}` `` against the pages, the files in `public/`, the GET routes of the modules under `src/api/` and those of the app's Elysia instance once it is registered (see Project setup), as are the paths given to `ctx.redirect` in pages and actions and to a guard's `redirect`; a path may be spelled as written or percent-encoded, `/café` or `/caf%C3%A9`; a catch-all such as `docs/[...path]`, or an app route such as `/files/*`, is reached with a trailing slash, `/docs/`, never as `/docs`; a template literal whose start or end is interpolated may reach any page it fits; a plain `string`, relative paths, `//host` and other schemes are not checked.
- Form field names against the action schema.
- Island props passed from static components can be serialized: no functions or class instances.
- No component reads a browser-only global while it renders, and no island branches on `typeof window` (see Browser-only components). Reported by `kay check` and the editor only, with quick fixes in the editor.
- Every content collection entry against its schema and the components its collection names, reported at the entry's line.
- With `i18n`, every `t()` key and its placeholders against the default locale's messages, and every other locale's messages against them: a key one lacks or has alone, a placeholder it drops or adds, plural forms where the default has text. Links may carry a locale's prefix.
- What a page needs to be usable without seeing it: an `img` has `alt` (`alt=""` for decoration), an `iframe` a `title`, an `input(type="image")` an `alt`, and an element with `onClick` is one a keyboard reaches, such as a `button` or an `a`, or has a `role`. An element with a `{...spread}` is not checked. These are reported by `kay check` and the editor only: the page still runs meanwhile.

## Project setup

kay is published as `@kaynooo/kayjs` to the registry at `https://git.kaynooo.fr/api/packages/kaynooo/npm/` and installed under the name its imports use: `"kay": "npm:@kaynooo/kayjs@^<version>"` in `package.json`, with `@kaynooo:registry=https://git.kaynooo.fr/api/packages/kaynooo/npm/` in the project's `.npmrc`. `bunx -p @kaynooo/kayjs kay new my-app` writes a project that already checks, builds and runs, both of those included: this setup, a layout, a page, a `_404.kay` and islands (see Commands for the templates). By hand, the server entry is:

```ts
import { Elysia } from 'elysia'
import { pages } from 'kay/server'

const app = new Elysia().get('/feed.xml', feed).use(await pages()).listen(3000)

declare module 'kay' {
  interface Register {
    app: typeof app
  }
}
```

Registering `app` lets links and redirects point at the app's own GET routes, such as `/feed.xml`, which `kay check` otherwise reports as served by no page.

Project settings live in an optional `kay.config.ts` at the root, read by `pages()` and every command; options passed to `pages()` win over it, unless `undefined`. It must `export default` its config, or the command fails with a message saying so.

```ts
import { defineConfig } from 'kay/server'

export default defineConfig({ routes: 'src/routes', lang: 'en', minify: true, prefetch: 'moderate', plugins: [] })
```

Every page carries speculation rules, which the swap replaces on pages shipping its script (see Navigation): Chromium prefetches the page a link points at once it is hovered (`prefetch: 'moderate'`), on press with `'conservative'`, as soon as it can with `'eager'`, never with `false`. A link that changes something on GET, such as a logout, takes `data-no-prefetch`. A stylesheet holding `@view-transition { navigation: auto; }` animates from page to page where the browser supports it, swaps included; `kay new` writes one.

`pages()` also takes `root`, `dev` (default: `NODE_ENV` is `development`) and `prebuilt` (default: `NODE_ENV` is `production`), which serves what `kay build` wrote instead of bundling at boot. A `.ts` file imports a component as `import Card from './card.kay'`, typed through the generated `.kay/types` tree. `.kay/` also holds the client build and the compile cache. List it in `.gitignore` and merge the tree in `tsconfig.json`:

```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "jsx": "preserve",
    "jsxImportSource": "kay",
    "module": "Preserve",
```
