```json
    "moduleResolution": "bundler",
    "rootDirs": [".", ".kay/types"],
    "strict": true
  },
  "include": ["src", ".kay/types"]
}
```

## Redirects

`redirects` in kay.config.ts sends old paths elsewhere, with a 308, or a 307 when `permanent` is false:

```ts
export default defineConfig({
  redirects: {
    '/blog/:slug': '/posts/:slug',
    '/docs/*': '/guide/*',
    '/sale': { to: 'https://shop.example.com/sale', permanent: false },
  },
})
```

- An old path names params as `:name` segments and may end in `*`; its target uses them, the `*` carrying the rest of the path, and the request's query goes along unless the target has its own. A target naming a param the old path lacks, or an old path a page serves, stops the server.
- `kay check` reports a target on the site that no page or public file serves; a `:param` stands for any segment there, and another site's URL is not checked.

## Static export

`kay build --static` writes the site to `dist`, or `--outdir`, for any static host: Forgejo Pages, a CDN, plain nginx.

- Every page is rendered: one without params as it is, one with params for the values its `prerender` lists. A page a guard covers, one exporting an action, one with params and no list, one exporting `prerender = false`, one that redirects or answers another status than 200, one linking an image only the image route makes, and one whose render fails cannot be served without a server, nor can a module under `src/api/`, and the build fails naming each of them.
- Each page is written as `about.html` and `about/index.html`, so a host finds it at `/about` and `/about/` alike, `/` as `index.html`; the browser build goes under `_kay/`, the public files at the root, with the sitemap, `robots.txt`, feeds, favicons and `404.html` from `_404.kay`. Every compressible file has its `.br` and `.gz` copy beside it, for a server sending them as they are (nginx's `gzip_static`), and asset names carry their hash, so `_kay/` can be cached forever.
- Imported images link the variants the build writes, `/_kay/images/hero-640.webp`, since no image route answers; an image from `images.dirs` is not exported.
- A redirect without params becomes a page sending the browser on with `<meta http-equiv="refresh">`; every redirect also goes to `_redirects`, read by hosts such as Netlify and Cloudflare Pages. With `i18n.prefixDefault`, each unprefixed path sends the browser to the default locale's copy. Locales by domain need a server.
- The directory is cleared first, only when the last export wrote it: kay refuses one holding other files, and the project itself.

## Base path

`base: '/docs'` in kay.config.ts mounts the site under a path of its host, as Pages does under `/<owner>/<repo>`. Links stay written without it, `a(href="/about")`: kay puts every root-relative `href`, `src`, `srcset`, `action`, `formaction`, `poster` and `data` a page renders under it, with inline `<style>` and stylesheet `url()`s, redirects (`Location`), canonical and `hreflang` links, the sitemap, `robots.txt`, feeds and the web manifest. A route starting like the base is no exception: under `base: '/blog'`, `a(href="/blog/hello")` goes to `/blog/blog/hello`. A server under `base` sits behind a proxy taking the path off requests: kay's routes stay at the root. What a script builds in the browser, such as a link an island makes, goes through `withBase('/about')` from `kay`, which leaves a path as it is on the server, where kay adds the base itself; island actions, their redirects and `localize()` do already.

## Rewrites

`rewrite` in kay.config.ts serves a request from another path, the browser keeping its URL, such as one host's pages from a section of the routes:

```ts
export default defineConfig({
  rewrite: url => url.hostname === 'shop.example.com' ? `/shop${url.pathname}${url.search}` : undefined,
})
```

- It returns a path starting with one `/`, query included, or `undefined` to serve the request as it came; anything else answers 500 and is logged. kay's own `/_kay/` routes, assets, actions, images and the health route, are never rewritten, so they work on every host.
- The rewritten request goes through the whole app again, the app's own routes, derives and guards included, and everything there sees the new path: `ctx.url`, `ctx.params`, links a page builds from them. It is not rewritten twice, and keeps its method, headers, cookies and body. Rate limits still count the client's own address. The request log shows the path it was rewritten to.
- Under `app.handle()` with no listening server, as in a test, only kay's pages serve a rewritten request.

## Request logs

With NODE_ENV=production, every request kay or the app's routes registered after `.use(await pages())` answer is logged to stdout as one line: `GET /blog/hello 200 12ms`, the method, the path without its query string, which may carry tokens, the status, and the milliseconds until the response was made, a streamed one's headers. kay's own `/_kay/` routes, assets included, and the health route, wherever `health.path` puts it, are left out. `log` in kay.config.ts changes it: `'json'` writes one JSON object per line, `{ time, method, path, status, duration }`, for a log collector; a function receives each `{ method, path, status, duration }` entry instead; `true` logs outside production too, `false` never.

## Health and shutdown

`/_kay/health` answers `200 ok` while the server takes requests, for a load balancer or a container's health check. `health: { path: '/up', check: async () => await db.ping() }` in kay.config.ts moves it and adds a check: one returning `false`, throwing, or taking over 5 s answers 503, the error logged. `health: false` leaves the route out.

On SIGTERM or SIGINT, a server started with `.listen()` stops taking connections, lets open requests and streams finish, then runs the app's `onStop` hooks and exits with 0. New connections are refused from the signal on, so a load balancer stops sending any; a client on a connection kept alive gets 503 from the health route meanwhile. Requests still open after `shutdownTimeout` seconds, 10 by default, are closed and the process exits with 1. `kay dev` restarts at once instead.

## Background jobs

`schedule(cron, job)` and `background(work)` from `kay/server` are Elysia plugins, so a job runs in the server's process, from `.listen()` to the server stopping, once per process:

```ts
import { Elysia } from 'elysia'
import { background, pages, schedule } from 'kay/server'

new Elysia()
  .use(schedule('@hourly', async () => purgeExpiredCarts()))
  .use(schedule('30 2 * * MON', sendWeeklyReport, { tz: 'Europe/Paris' }))
  .use(background(async (signal) => {
    while (!signal.aborted)
      await handleNextEmail(signal)
  }))
  .use(await pages())
  .listen(3000)
```

- `schedule` takes five cron fields, `minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week`, or a nickname such as `@daily`, read in the system's time zone unless `tz` names one. One it cannot read, or one that never comes, fails the boot. Runs never overlap: the next is planned once the last settles. A run that throws is logged and the next one comes as planned.
- `background` starts `work` with the server, for a queue consumer or anything else that runs the whole time. On stop its signal aborts and the server waits for it to return. Work that throws is logged and not started again.
- Stopping on a signal waits for a scheduled run in progress, and for every `onStop` hook the app registers, async ones included, in turn. `shutDown(app)` from `kay/server` stops a server the same way, as a test does; Elysia's own `app.stop()` does not wait for the hooks.
- With several server processes, each runs its own schedules: a job that must run once overall belongs to one process only, or takes a lock.

## Security headers

Every response the app sends, its own routes included, carries a Content-Security-Policy, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin` and `X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN`. The policy:

```text
default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' <kay's hashes>; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data: https:; font-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'; frame-ancestors 'self'
```

Every inline script kay writes is the same on every page: the hydration bootstrap, the speculation rules, the swap of streamed blocks and, in development, live reload. The policy allows them by hash, with no `'unsafe-inline'` and no nonce. `security` in `kay.config.ts` adjusts it:

```ts
import { defineConfig } from 'kay/server'

export default defineConfig({
  security: {
    csp: { 'img-src': ['\'self\'', 'https://images.example.com'], 'frame-ancestors': false },
    headers: { 'strict-transport-security': 'max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains', 'x-frame-options': false },
  },
})
```

- `csp` merges directives over kay's, one given `false` left out; `script-src`, and `script-src-elem` when the app sets one, keep kay's hashes whatever they list. `'script-src': false` leaves kay's inline scripts to `default-src`, which blocks them, islands and streamed blocks with them. `csp: false` sends no policy, `security: false` none of these headers.
- `headers` merges headers over kay's, one given `false` not sent. HSTS is not sent by default: it binds the domain to https for its `max-age`, so it is the app's call.
- A header the app sets itself, in an Elysia `onRequest` or a handler, wins over kay's.
- `inlineScriptHashes({ prefetch, dev })` from `kay/server` gives the hashes, for a policy written elsewhere, such as by a proxy.

## Compression

With no proxy in front compressing responses, `compress: true` in kay.config.ts has kay do it: pages rendered per request, action results, and any `Response` the app's routes registered after `.use(await pages())` return go out with brotli or gzip, whichever the browser's `Accept-Encoding` prefers, and `Vary: Accept-Encoding`. A streamed page is flushed chunk by chunk, so what it sends early still arrives early. A strong ETag becomes weak. Left alone: a response encoded already, such as the build's copies, one under 256 bytes, one with `Cache-Control: no-transform`, and anything but text, JSON, JavaScript, XML and SVG.

## Commands

- `kay new <dir> [--kay <dependency>] [--template server|site|app]`: scaffold a project in an empty directory. Every template has a layout with `seo` defaults and a skip link, a header with an accent picker over the Catppuccin Mocha palette, kept in a cookie, Tailwind through `bun-plugin-tailwind`, and Tabler icons. `server`, the default, is an Elysia server, with a `Dockerfile` and `compose.prod.yaml` running the executable `bun run compile` makes. `site` is a static site whose `bun run build` runs `kay build --static`, its pages showing the default accent until the picker hydrates, since no server reads the cookie, with a Forgejo Pages workflow publishing `dist` to the `gitea-pages` branch under `/<owner>/<repo>` and a `Dockerfile` serving it with nginx instead. `app` is the server with sessions, a sign-in action, a guarded `/account` section, an API module and an island over its websocket, its session secret written to a `.env` git ignores, `.env.test` holding a test-only one so `bun test` runs in a fresh clone and CI, and `.env.example` naming what production sets; `--kay` sets the `kay` dependency, by default `npm:@kaynooo/kayjs@^<its version>`, or a packed copy when run from a checkout of kay. The package is named after the directory, lower case with other characters turned into `-`.
- `kay dev [entry]`: run the server entry (default `src/server.ts`) with `NODE_ENV=development`, restarting it on every change; open pages reload by themselves, or only swap their stylesheets when nothing but `.css` files changed, and a project that fails to compile shows its errors in the browser. When only island components changed, an open page swaps each edited island in place, and each island rendering it inside, instead of reloading: the rest of the page, its other islands and its form fields stay as they were. The swapped island is built afresh, so what it does not hold in signals, such as an unbound input's text or the focus inside it, starts over; the signals its script creates keep their values, matched in the order it creates them, until one whose initial value is of another kind, as after adding a signal before it. Signals made inside a `for` row, an `if` or `await` block, or by kay itself start afresh; two signals of one kind swapped in the script trade values. A change to anything else, a page, a layout, a static component, a `.ts` module or a deleted source file, an island that failed to hydrate, a new chunk holding code the page already runs, or a page that missed a restart, reloads as before. Island chunks carry source maps, so the browser's devtools show and break on `.kay` lines. The next server process waits with kay already loaded, and compiled files are kept in `.kay/cache`, so a restart compiles only the file that changed. A change to a file at the project root, such as `.env` or `package.json`, starts a fresh process, which reads the new `.env` values (variables set in the shell still win, unless they equal the file's value).
- `kay build [dir]`: bundle the islands and stylesheets for production, minified, into `.kay/client`, and render the pages marked `prerender`; then start the server with `NODE_ENV=production`. Each page preloads the chunks of the islands it renders. Every text file it writes, prerendered pages included, gets a brotli and a gzip copy, sent to a browser whose `Accept-Encoding` takes one, with `Vary: Accept-Encoding`; other responses go uncompressed, left to a proxy in front, unless `compress` is on.
- `kay build [dir] --compile <executable> [--entry src/server.ts]`: the same, then bundles the server entry, every page, layout, special page, guard and API module, `kay.config.ts` and the client build and public files into one executable, which runs from anywhere as the production server would: `PORT=8080 ./server`. It reads nothing of the project from disk but a `.env` and `bunfig.toml` where it runs, as `bun` would, so a file a page reads at runtime by path, rather than importing it, is not in it; the root, routes and public directory it was built with win over the options given to `pages()`. `--compile` and `--entry` are relative to the current directory. The public directory cannot be named `client`.
- `kay build [dir] --static [--outdir dist]`: the same, then writes the whole site to `--outdir` for a host with no server; see Static export.
- `kay check [dir] [-p tsconfig.json]`: type-check the project, `.kay` files included; `-p` is relative to `dir`, and a tsconfig that is missing or matches no files fails the check.
- `kay fmt [paths...] [--check]`: format `.kay` files; `--check` lists unformatted files and fails.
- `kay lsp --stdio`: the language server behind the editor extension in `editors/vscode`: errors, hover, completion with auto-import, signatures, definitions, references, rename, quick fixes and formatting in `.kay` files. An import it adds goes in the fence the name is used from, the server fence for server code and the component script otherwise, made if missing. Renaming a server value renames its reads in the template, and renaming a destructured prop renames it in every parent passing it.

Every command prints its usage for `--help` or `-h`, and refuses an option or argument it does not take. `kay fmt` refuses a path that is missing or is neither a directory nor a `.kay` file.
